Consider the vector field $F=⟨y-z,\,y-2x,\,x+4z⟩$ and the surface $S$ defined by the bounding region of the rectangular solid shown above in the first octant. Given that $S$ is positively (outward) oriented, use the divergence theorem to find the flux of $F$ through $S.$
question.worked_solution:
Let $R$ be a simple solid region bounded by a closed surface $S$ with positive (outward) orientation. If a vector field $F$ has continuous partial derivatives for all its components in an open region in space that contains $R,$ then the divergence theorem states that

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot dS={∭}_{R}\text{div}\,F\,\text{d}V.
$$

Computing the divergence of $F,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{div}\,F & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(y-z)+\frac{∂}{∂y}(y-2x)+\frac{∂}{∂z}(x+4z) \\  & =0+1+4 \\  & =5.\end{aligned}
$$

Let $R$ be the rectangular solid enclosed by $S.$ Then, using the divergence theorem, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}F\cdot dS & ={∭}_{R}5\,\text{d}V \\  & =5{∭}_{R}\,\text{d}V \\  & =5\cdot \text{Volume}(R) \\  & =5\cdot 4\cdot 2\cdot 2 \\  & =80.\end{aligned}
$$
